dedupe_keys.name: national neighborhood data archive nanda broadband availability speed and internet access by census tract and zip code

description: The National Neighborhood Data Archive at the University of Michigan, distributed through ICPSR, publishes neighbourhood-level measures of internet infrastructure for the United States by census tract and ZIP Code Tabulation Area. The broadband availability series, derived from providers' reports to the FCC Broadband Data Collection, gives for 2025 the number of providers, the share of housing units and land area with access, download and upload speed tiers (from under 10 to over 2,000 Mbps), unserved, underserved and served categories (25/3 and 100/20 Mbps thresholds), low-latency service and technology shares (fibre, cable, copper, fixed wireless, satellite). Earlier series cover broadband availability, speed and adoption from the FCC Form 477 and internet access from the American Community Survey. Coverage: all US tracts and ZCTAs, by year. Format and access: CSV and Stata files with codebooks at ICPSR, free of charge for research after a free login. Caveats: availability reported by providers overstates service; adoption and availability come from different sources; tract averages hide gaps. Simulation uses: neighbourhood connectivity for social vulnerability weighting of outages, exposure of unserved areas, and equity analysis. Related records: FCC Form 477 and the NTIA Internet Use Survey.
